title: George Foreman
wiki_lead:
George Edward Foreman (January 10, 1949 – March 21, 2025) was an American professional boxer, businessman, minister, and author. In boxing, he competed between 1967 and 1997, and was nicknamed "Big George". He was a two-time world heavyweight champion and an Olympic gold medalist. He is the namesake of the George Foreman Grill.
After a troubled childhood, Foreman took up amateur boxing and won a gold medal in the heavyweight division at the 1968 Summer Olympics. Having turned professional the next year, he won the undisputed world heavyweight title with a stunning second-round knockout of the then-undefeated Joe Frazier in 1973. He defended the belt twice before suffering his first professional loss to Muhammad Ali in "The Rumble in the Jungle" in 1974. Unable to secure another title opportunity, Foreman retired after a loss to Jimmy Young in 1977.
Following what he referred to as a born again experience, Foreman became an ordained Christian minister. Ten years later he announced a comeback, and in 1994, at age 45, won the unified WBA, IBF, and lineal heavyweight championship titles by knocking out 26-year-old Michael Moorer, earning Associated Press Athlete of the Year honors. He dropped the WBA belt rather than face his mandatory title defense soon after, and following a single successful title defense against Axel Schulz, Foreman relinquished his IBF title as well on June 28, 1995. At 46 years and 169 days old, he became the oldest world heavyweight champion in history, as well as the second-oldest boxer to win a world title in any weight class after Bernard Hopkins at light heavyweight. Foreman also holds the record for the longest interval between world title reigns, spanning more than 20 years. He retired in 1997 at the age of 48, with a final record of 76 wins (68 knockouts) and 5 losses.
Foreman is a member of both the World Boxing Hall of Fame and the International Boxing Hall of Fame. The International Boxing Research Organization rates Foreman as the eighth-greatest heavyweight of all time. In 2002, he was named one of the 25 greatest fighters of the past 80 years by The Ring; the following year, the magazine ranked him as the ninth-greatest puncher of all time. He was a ringside analyst for HBO's boxing coverage for 12 years until 2004. Outside boxing, Foreman was a successful entrepreneur and known for his promotion of the George Foreman Grill, which had sold more than 100 million units worldwide by 2011. In 1999, he sold the commercial rights to the grill for $138 million.

grok_lead: George Foreman (January 10, 1949 â March 21, 2025) was an American professional boxer, ordained minister, entrepreneur, and author, best known for his two heavyweight world championships, Olympic gold medal, and the endorsement of the iconic George Foreman Grill that generated hundreds of millions in revenue. Born in Marshall, Texas, and raised in the impoverished Fifth Ward neighborhood of Houston, Foreman grew up as the fifth of seven children in a single-parent household led by his mother, Nancy Ree, after his biological father, Leroy Moorehead, was absent. He dropped out of school at age 15 and engaged in petty crime, including mugging, before joining the Job Corps at 16, where he learned boxing under trainer Doc Broaddus and developed skills in carpentry and bricklaying. His amateur career culminated in a gold medal at the 1968 Summer Olympics in Mexico City, where he defeated the Soviet Union's Jonas Äepulis in the heavyweight division, raising a small American flag in celebration, an act that drew controversy amid the era's racial tensions and the Black Power protests. Foreman turned professional in 1969 and quickly rose to prominence with a 37-fight winning streak, all by knockout, showcasing his devastating punching power at 6 feet 3 inches tall with an 78.5-inch reach. He captured the undisputed heavyweight title on January 22, 1973, by stopping Joe Frazier in the second round in Kingston, Jamaica, knocking him down six times in what became known as the "Sunshine Showdown." His reign ended dramatically on October 30, 1974, when Muhammad Ali defeated him by eighth-round knockout in the "Rumble in the Jungle" in Kinshasa, Zaire, using the rope-a-dope strategy. After further losses, including to Jimmy Young in 1977, Foreman retired and experienced a profound religious conversion, becoming an ordained minister in 1978 and founding the Church of the Lord Jesus Christ in Houston in 1980. He also established the George Foreman Youth and Community Center in 1984 to aid at-risk youth in Houston's Fifth Ward. In a remarkable comeback at age 38, Foreman returned to boxing in 1987, motivated by his ministry work, and amassed a 24-1 record in his second career phase, culminating in a stunning 10th-round knockout of Michael Moorer on November 5, 1994, to reclaim the WBA and IBF heavyweight titles at age 45âthe oldest champion in any weight class in boxing history. He was inducted into the International Boxing Hall of Fame in 2003. His professional record stood at 76 wins (68 by knockout), 5 losses upon retiring in 1997. Beyond the ring, Foreman built a vast family with 12 childrenâincluding five sons all named Georgeâand four wives, emphasizing faith and forgiveness in his personal life. His entrepreneurial success came from endorsing the George Foreman Grill, invented by Michael Boehm in 1994; Foreman signed a deal in 1999 that netted him over $200 million, turning the fat-reducing appliance into a global bestseller with over 100 million units sold. Foreman passed away on March 21, 2025, at age 76 in Houston, Texas, as announced by his family; the cause was not publicly disclosed. Throughout his later years, he remained active in preaching four times weekly at his church, authored books on faith and boxing, and maintained a close friendship with Ali, serving as a pallbearer at Ali's 2016 funeral. Foreman's life exemplified reinvention, from street tough to Olympic hero, two-time world champion, devout pastor, and business icon, leaving a legacy of resilience and redemption.
